note: Tempdoc 600 PART IX/X — the degradation-cause reason vocabulary is ONE closed authority. The producer (StatusLifecycleHandler) emits readiness reason codes from the closed LifecycleReasonCode enum; the FE CAUSE_ROWS table words them (code -> wording/remedy/severity). This register's gate (scripts/ci/check-readiness-reason-codes.mjs) enforces producer<->consumer correspondence so neither can drift: FORWARD = every enum code that is NOT exempt has a CAUSE_ROWS row (so a user can never be shown a raw `Degraded: <code>` string in the degradation banner); BACKWARD = every CAUSE_ROWS code is a real enum member OR a declared FE-derived code (no dead/typo rows); PRODUCER (tempdoc 837 §5) = every enum code is referenced by at least one modules/**/src/main Java source outside the enum's own file, by enum NAME or quoted code string, matched AFTER comment-stripping. The two allow-lists below are the only curated artifact (the search-issuance gate's allowedReferences pattern); note that noWordingExempt does NOT exempt from the PRODUCER direction, since the two lists answer different questions (a code can legitimately never reach the banner and still need an emit site).
producerDirectionNote: Tempdoc 837 §4/§5. Four ORT_CUDA_* codes lived in this vocabulary with no producer for months, two of them carrying user-facing wording for a state that could not occur; S1 deleted them and S2 added the direction that makes the class unrepresentable. Post-S1 all 44 codes have an emit-site reference, so the PRODUCER direction runs with an EMPTY effective exemption — there is deliberately no new allow-list. If a future code appears to need one, that is a design conversation, not a one-line entry. KNOWN UNCOVERED SEAM (837 §5.4): a reference is not an emission (a consumer's `X.code().equals(...)` satisfies the check), and tap coverage is separate — a code can have an emit site, a wording row, and still produce no Condition, because LifecycleSnapshotTap's (dimension, state, code) rows are not registered anywhere. Closing that needs a triple register and is not built.

noWordingExempt.why: Fail-closed boot refusal (tempdoc 884 item 23): the Head throws at LocalApiServer construction before the loopback bind, so no readiness envelope, ConditionStore or SSE stream exists to carry it. The operator sees it in the fatal log line and the process exit; there is no UI to word it in.

Head-owned ConditionStore condition (SettingsRecoveryNotice, tempdoc 882 item 24); never on the readiness envelope, so never reaches wordCauses. The user sees it on the Health surface, which renders conditions with the Java-side message.
NOT_CONFIGURED state on INDEX_SERVING -> verdict 'checking', never rendered by wordCauses (PART X)
NOT_READY state on INDEX_SERVING -> verdict 'checking' (reproduced live: no banner)
TELEMETRY dimension -> 'telemetry' composite, which the verdict never reads

feDerived.why: Tempdoc 596 §17 — FE-only control-availability code; not emitted by the readiness producer

emissionDirectionNote: Lane F stage A checkpoint. checkProducers asks whether a code is MENTIONED; checkEmissions asks whether it is PRODUCED — mentioned in a value position rather than only compared against or logged. The weaker question let two passes of a design document disagree about whether WORKER_RESTART_EXHAUSTED had a producer while this gate certified both. awaitingProducer is the declared escape hatch: a code whose producer is scheduled but unwritten stays visible and owned instead of being indistinguishable from a live one. The gate also reds when a declared entry gains a producer, so the list cannot rot into a permanent exemption.

awaitingProducer.why: Lane F stage A deleted the Worker process and with it the only thing that could give up on restarting it. All four main-source sites are consumers: KnowledgeServerBootstrap.java:444-447 and KnowledgeServerHealthMonitor.java:342-344 compare it against pendingReason(); KnowledgeServerBootstrap.java:729-732 and KnowledgeServerHealthMonitor.java:498-500 pass it to a logger. Nothing transitions to it, so supervisionVerdictHeld() is permanently false and BootRecoveryDecision SUPERVISION_ENGAGED plus its terminal-verdict branch are inert. Kept rather than deleted because design 7.1 lands a real supervisor with a kill path and a restart budget at stage B, which is the producer. Stage B clears this entry by adding the emit site.
